title:
From citation
to decision.
consentText: This university study explores how people check AI-generated research statements against original sources. You will review eight statements in approximately 10–15 minutes. We record your choices, response times, source-opening and page interactions, language, and interruptions under an anonymous study ID. We do not ask for your name or student ID. The papers are in English. Participation is voluntary; you may stop without penalty.
agree: I am 18 or older and freely agree to participate.
declined: You have not joined the study. No trial data or participant ID was created.
instructionsText:
Imagine you are a university researcher preparing a short research summary.

An AI research assistant has suggested eight statements from published research papers.

Your task is to check whether each statement is supported by its original source before deciding to use it.

welcomeDescription:
Take part in a university research study about how people check information suggested by AI.

You will review eight research statements, check their original sources, and decide whether you would include each statement in a research summary.
stepsText: Decide whether to include the statement exactly as written.
decisionDefinitions:
Include as written = The source supports the statement.
Do not include as written = The source does not support the statement.
instructionsEnd: There is no time limit. You may reopen sources as often as needed. Base your decisions on the evidence. You will not receive correctness feedback.
decisionQuestion: Would you include this statement in your research summary exactly as written?

descriptions.CS: This study investigated how people use smartphones in freezing weather. Researchers asked participants about their phone activities and the problems they experienced in cold conditions.
descriptions.RB: This study explored how people interact with robots while doing another activity. Researchers compared two ways of delivering objects: handing them directly to people or placing them on a nearby table.
descriptions.EC: This study examined how different suggested donation amounts might influence people's decisions to donate money at a restaurant.
descriptions.ED: This study compared two versions of an online learning platform. One included game features, such as points and levels, while the other did not.
